VI.description: Rule probe for LV009, written 2026-10-23 for research round 10. Five terminals that separate what the two checkers are each responsible for: error in as required and error out as optional, both with NO conIdx (LV009's own gaps); error out 2 as recommended (must be silent); and error out 3 as required WITH a conIdx, which upstream's conn-required-output owns, so LV009 must stay silent there. Two decoys guard against over-reach: an ordinary input marked required, and a control whose name starts with 'Last'. Tests the checker, not LabVIEW: never converted.

Control.description: LV009's gap: no conIdx, so the vendored lint's conn-error-in-not-recommended cannot fire (its author measured the conIdx case). Must be an ERROR here.
Decoy: an ordinary input the caller must legitimately supply. The rule must NOT touch this one.
Decoy: not an error terminal despite the word. The pattern is anchored at the start of the name, so this is silent.

Indicator.description: LV009's other gap: a required output is upstream's business, an optional one was nobody's. Must be a WARNING here.
Correct spelling. Must be silent in both checkers.
Boundary: the same fault as a required output, but WITH a conIdx, so upstream's conn-required-output reports it and LV009 must not.
